exact_statement: For every uniform Boolean OR of gates each combining at most M regular functions, the disjoint least-pivotal-gate derivative partition defines normalized laws nu_j and rho_j. For every kappa_j>=1, epsilon_j=sum_T(nu_j(T)-kappa_j*rho_j(T))_+, E_nu_j G_j <= E0+(24/5)log2(M*kappa_j)+epsilon_j*Gmax_j, where E0=(24/5)[log2(sqrt(2e)+2^(3/5))+log2 e]. For the source-component forest with global root odds lambda*pi_l, 0<lambda<=1, the explicit congestion Gamma in REPORT equation (2) yields H(f)<=[K0+E0+(29/5)log2 M+Gamma]I(f), with every root/label/subset/normalization cost retained. Addressing on a selectors has read 2^a, kappa_j<=2, epsilon_j=0, Gamma<3/4+24/5 and H<=50I for all integers a>=1; this is a known class calibration. For the projective-plane line union over any prime q with delta_q=(q^2+q)2^(-q)<1, worst-event derivative congestion is at least (q+1)(1-delta_q)^2, hence is unbounded. Least-gate masses lie between 2^(-q)(1-delta_q) and 2^(-q). More generally, ideal pieces with disjoint Fourier supports outside E certify epsilon_j(4)<=nu_j(E)+(4*sum_l||a_l-d_jl||_2^2+2*||sum_l(a_l-d_jl)||_2^2)/alpha_j. On PP_q this gives epsilon_j(4)*Gmax_j<=308/5 for every prime q, and sum_j alpha_j E_nu_j G_j<93 I(PP_q). The complete PP root/label/subset payment and universal FEI remain open.
